newsitem.title: UK: NWE naphtha ends firm by hooking onto gasoline buoy.
newsitem.headline: NWE naphtha ends firm by hooking onto gasoline buoy.

text.p: NWE naphtha prices ended steady on Wednesday with traders looking to the seasonal gasoline market as a primary lifejacket in the face of lacklustre end-user demand and ample local supplies.

"The only strength for naphtha will come either from the arb opening to the West or East or gasoline booming up and that will take naphtha production out of the refinery," said one Scandanavian trader.
"N+A is definitely in demand at the moment because of the gasoline," she said, referring to the heavier naphthenic and aromatic naphtha, a feedstock for reformers to make gasoline.
May swaps ended 50 cents higher at $181.50/$182.50 a tonne with June at $183.50/$184.50 and July at $184/$185.
The spot NYMEX gasoline contract hit a four-week high on Wednesday, gaining nearly two cents a gallon in the last two sessions ahead of the May's expiry later today.
Cargo prices were notionally valued at $180/$182 cif where some bids were heard earlier, but not heard completed.
"No end-users are buying spot volumes because they are just covered on contracts," the trader said.
